class.name: FrameBudget
class.brief_description: Says what made a frame long, and spreads heavy work over frames.
class.description: Time named pieces of your game's heavy work with [method measure]. A frame that takes longer than [member long_frame_ms] prints what took its time, so "it's sometimes slow" names its cause: [codeblock] Long frame: 63 ms (city 30.4 ms, traffic 12.1 ms; the rest drawing and the engine's own). [/codeblock] Work that can wait (building collision, loading the next part of a world) runs a slice at a time with [method spread], within a budget each frame, and with more of it while [member screen_hidden] says nobody sees a slow frame. Reports are on in debug builds (except headless, where frames draw nothing); in release builds, set [code]frame_budget/report_in_release_builds[/code] or turn on [member reporting] (for a playtest build, say).

method.name: get_spread_count
method.description: How many jobs [method spread] is still running.

method.name: measure
method.description: Counts the time since [param since_usec] (from [method Time.get_ticks_usec]) to [param what], in this frame's report. Measuring costs nothing while [member reporting] is off. [codeblock] var started := Time.get_ticks_usec() build_paths() FrameBudget.measure("paths", started) [/codeblock]

method.name: spread

members.member: A frame taking at least this long (milliseconds) is reported. Starts from [code]frame_budget/long_frame_ms[/code].
Whether long frames are reported and work is measured. On in debug builds unless headless, and in release builds with [code]frame_budget/report_in_release_builds[/code].
Set while nobody can see a slow frame (a fade to black, a loading screen): work spread with [method spread] gets six times its budget meanwhile.

signal.name: long_frame
signal.description: A frame took [param milliseconds], at least [member long_frame_ms]. [param work] is what was measured in it, by name, in milliseconds. Emitted for every long frame, though the log has one a second at most.
